study.title: perfDSA: Automatic Perfusion Imaging in Cerebral Digital Subtraction Angiography
study.venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery

imaging.modality_detail: Cerebral 2D+time DSA series, AP or lateral views; initial temporal resolution 2-4 frames per second
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebral; supraclinoid ICA as input artery; ICA and MCA territories in acute ischemic stroke after thrombectomy

public_dataset_used.detail: MR CLEAN Registry (nationwide multicenter observational cohort, Netherlands); not described as publicly downloadable

task.task_description: Fully automatic deconvolution-based perfusion parametric imaging (CBV, CBF, MTT, Tmax) from cerebral DSA, using UNet segmentation of the supraclinoid ICA to extract the arterial input function; perfusion parameters then used to predict functional stroke outcome via logistic regression.
task.clinical_application: Quantitative perfusion assessment during endovascular thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke; biomarkers for functional outcome

temporal_evidence.quote: This approach involves deconvolving time–intensity curves (TICs) using the extracted AIF.

metrics.metric: Perfusion parametric image generation runtime per series

comparators: Manual AIF extraction from manually annotated input artery masks

G3.quote: the temporal flow dynamics are generally not intuitively visualized and explained in such methods

G4.quote: The lack of automatic approaches for reliable assessment of cerebral flow dynamics might be partially due to the projective nature of DSA.

G5.quote: As the annotations were created by a single individual, interannotator variability was not quantitatively assessed.

G6.quote: These interesting initial findings necessitate further large-scale clinical validations.

G11.quote: this work also investigates the association between quantitative perfusion parameters and functional stroke outcomes after endovascular stroke treatment

other_limitations: Full quantitative accuracy of DSA perfusion parameters not confirmed
Segmentation tends to under-segment the target vessel (sensitivity 79%)
Off-target segmentations due to motion artifacts or static instruments
High boundary uncertainty in manual annotations of small target segment
future_work: Enhance perfDSA with state-of-the-art segmentation models (e.g., nnUNet, CAVE)
Validate DSA-derived perfusion parameters against MRA in the same patient cohort
Large-scale clinical studies to assess associations with outcomes
